def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : Type) (P : S2 X Y) (T : ℕ),
    ∃ N : S1 X Y, N.D9 ∧ N.d13 = T ∧
      ∀ xs : List X, xs.length ≤ T → N.d4 xs = P.d4 xs

{"translation": "Target defines a proposition (it does not assert or prove it) stating the following: For all types X and Y, for every system P of type S2 X Y, and for every natural number T, there exists a system N of type S1 X Y (which may depend on X, Y, P, and T) satisfying three conditions:

1. Acyclicity of state-update dependencies (N.D9): Let D8 be the binary relation on N's finite index type N.A1 where D8 m n holds if and only if there exist two global states σ, σ' : (k : N.A1) → N.A3 k and an input x : X such that σ k = σ' k for all k ≠ m and N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x (i.e., changing only component m's state can change component n's next state for some input x). Then for every n : N.A1, there is no chain n = c0, c1, ..., ck = n of length k ≥ 1 with D8 c_i c_{i+1} at each step (so D8 has no directed cycles of length ≥ 1, including self-loops).

2. Exact component count (N.d13 = T): The cardinality of the finite type N.A1 is exactly T (not merely at most T).

3. Output agreement up to length T: For every finite list xs of elements of X with xs.length ≤ T, N.d4 xs = P.d4 xs.

Here:
- A system P : S2 X Y consists of two arbitrary types B1 and B2, initial values b3 : B1 and b4 : B2, transition functions b5 : B1 → B2 → X → B2 and b6 : B1 → B2 → X → B1, and an output function a6 : B2 → Y. Starting from (b3, b4), P processes a list xs : List X from left to right by simultaneously updating (s1, s2) on input x to (b6 s1 s2 x, b5 s1 s2 x), and P.d4 xs applies P.a6 to the final B2 component.
- A system N : S1 X Y consists of a finite type A1, a family of arbitrary types A3 : A1 → Type, an initial global state a4 : (n : A1) → A3 n, a component update function a5 : (n : A1) → ((m : A1) → A3 m) → X → A3 n, and an output function a6 : ((m : A1) → A3 m) → Y. Starting from a4, N processes xs : List X from left to right by synchronously updating global state σ on input x to (fun n => a5 n σ x), and N.d4 xs applies N.a6 to the resulting global state.

What is not required: X, Y, P.B1, P.B2, and the component state types N.A3 n are not required to be finite or nonempty; no computability or structural restriction is placed on the functions a5 and a6 beyond typing; N and P are not required to agree on input lists of length strictly greater than T, nor on anything other than their outputs in Y; and D9 depends only on semantic sensitivity of N.a5 (which is vacuous if X is empty)."}
translation:
Target defines a proposition (it does not assert or prove it) stating the following: For all types X and Y, for every system P of type S2 X Y, and for every natural number T, there exists a system N of type S1 X Y (which may depend on X, Y, P, and T) satisfying three conditions:

1. Acyclicity of state-update dependencies (N.D9): Let D8 be the binary relation on N's finite index type N.A1 where D8 m n holds if and only if there exist two global states σ, σ' : (k : N.A1) → N.A3 k and an input x : X such that σ k = σ' k for all k ≠ m and N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x (i.e., changing only component m's state can change component n's next state for some input x). Then for every n : N.A1, there is no chain n = c0, c1, ..., ck = n of length k ≥ 1 with D8 c_i c_{i+1} at each step (so D8 has no directed cycles of length ≥ 1, including self-loops).

2. Exact component count (N.d13 = T): The cardinality of the finite type N.A1 is exactly T (not merely at most T).

3. Output agreement up to length T: For every finite list xs of elements of X with xs.length ≤ T, N.d4 xs = P.d4 xs.

Here:
- A system P : S2 X Y consists of two arbitrary types B1 and B2, initial values b3 : B1 and b4 : B2, transition functions b5 : B1 → B2 → X → B2 and b6 : B1 → B2 → X → B1, and an output function a6 : B2 → Y. Starting from (b3, b4), P processes a list xs : List X from left to right by simultaneously updating (s1, s2) on input x to (b6 s1 s2 x, b5 s1 s2 x), and P.d4 xs applies P.a6 to the final B2 component.
- A system N : S1 X Y consists of a finite type A1, a family of arbitrary types A3 : A1 → Type, an initial global state a4 : (n : A1) → A3 n, a component update function a5 : (n : A1) → ((m : A1) → A3 m) → X → A3 n, and an output function a6 : ((m : A1) → A3 m) → Y. Starting from a4, N processes xs : List X from left to right by synchronously updating global state σ on input x to (fun n => a5 n σ x), and N.d4 xs applies N.a6 to the resulting global state.

What is not required: X, Y, P.B1, P.B2, and the component state types N.A3 n are not required to be finite or nonempty; no computability or structural restriction is placed on the functions a5 and a6 beyond typing; N and P are not required to agree on input lists of length strictly greater than T, nor on anything other than their outputs in Y; and D9 depends only on semantic sensitivity of N.a5 (which is vacuous if X is empty).

divergences.description: Polarity and mischaracterization of the unrefuted finite-horizon case: [P-O1] and [P-O3] assert that under plasticity, premise P2 is invalidated and functional equivalence breaks for all t > t0 (including finite horizons), and [P-O1] only concedes finite-horizon functional equivalence 'with fixed parameters'. Target instead asserts that finite-horizon equivalence holds for every plastic system P : S2 X Y. While the author frames Target as testing whether plasticity invalidates P2, characterizing Target as 'the finite-horizon equivalence that O'Reilly-Shah et al. say they do not refute' drops the 'with fixed parameters' restriction from [P-O1].

Different notion of functional equivalence and stateful S1 versus 'static FNN': [P-O3] evaluates equivalence between an RNN whose instantaneous input-output mapping changes over time t > t0 and a 'static' FNN whose mapping does not change over time. Target (as declared) instead defines equivalence on the map from the whole input history xs : List X (length ≤ T) to Y, and models the feedforward system N : S1 X Y as a T-dependent, stateful discrete-time dynamical system (folding N.d2 over xs, with every unit receiving the current input x and passing state forward along an acyclic graph N.D9). Because N maintains evolving internal state across steps—and can carry P's changing parameter state inside its own unit states—it is not a static FNN in the sense of [P-O3].

Unconstrained abstract state machines (S1, S2) instead of neural networks (RNNs/FNNs): [P-O1] and [P-O3] specifically concern RNNs, FNNs, network parameters, and 'the evolving nature of neural network functions'. In Lean, S1 and S2 have no neural-network architecture: unit state types (N.A3 n), system states (P.B2), and parameters (P.B1) are arbitrary Types, and update and readout functions (N.a5, N.a6, P.b5, P.b6, P.a6) are arbitrary mathematical functions. Crucially, because a single unit of N : S1 X Y can have an arbitrary state type (such as P.B1 × P.B2 or List X) and an arbitrary update function, one unit can store the entire state and plastic parameters of P (or the whole input history) and execute P's plasticity rule directly—making Target trivially provable while bypassing the neural-network claim in the source.

Restricted model of plasticity in S2: S2 models plasticity strictly as a deterministic, discrete-time, synchronous function P.b6 : B1 → B2 → X → B1 of current parameters, current state, and current input X, so it cannot express stochastic, continuous-time, or exogenous/unobserved parameter changes not determined by X. Structurally, P.B1 plays no distinct architectural role from P.B2 (and P.a6 : B2 → Y cannot directly depend on P.B1 without duplicating it into B2). Target also omits the qualifiers 'rapid' and 'nontrivial' plasticity, though because Target quantifies universally over all P : S2 X Y this strengthens rather than weakens the statement.

Added exact unit count (N.d13 = T): Neither [P-O1] nor [P-O3] mentions a feedforward network having exactly T units. Adding N.d13 = T strengthens the existential claim in Lean, and is only achievable independently of P's complexity because each unit of S1 can hold an arbitrarily rich state type N.A3 n rather than a scalar neuron.

judgement.summary: Target diverges materially from [P-O1] and [P-O3]: it asserts finite-horizon equivalence for plastic systems (whereas O'Reilly-Shah et al. only leave fixed-parameter finite-horizon equivalence unrefuted and claim plasticity breaks equivalence for all t > t0), replaces a static FNN matching instantaneous mappings with a stateful T-dependent pipeline matching history-to-output maps, and replaces neural networks with unconstrained abstract state machines whose single units can store P's entire plastic parameter space and execute its plasticity rule.
